existing_copy_for_context_only.short: Trump: Pentagon drops flu shot requirement for troops
existing_copy_for_context_only.medium: A May 29, 2025 memo from Deputy Defense Secretary Steve Feinberg changed when reserve troops were subject to the annual flu-shot requirement, setting a 30-day active-duty threshold. It did not remove the requirement for all troops. Its effect on vaccination-related pay is not clear from the description.
existing_copy_for_context_only.long: Deputy Defense Secretary Steve Feinberg’s May 29, 2025 memo set a threshold for when reserve troops on active duty would be required to receive an annual flu shot: 30 days or more of active-duty service. That is narrower than a blanket removal of the flu-shot requirement for all military personnel. The change concerned how the rule applied to reserve service and could affect people whose duty periods fell below the threshold. The timeline also alleges that the policy changed whether troops were paid when they received vaccination, but does not explain the compensation rules or how that consequence followed from the memo. The memo’s text is needed to identify the reserve categories covered and its effective date. Until those details are clear, the policy can be described as a change in the service threshold, not as a general end to vaccination requirements or a proven penalty for being vaccinated.

existing_copy_for_context_only.medium: Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. hired Lyn Redwood in June 2025 for an HHS role whose exact scope was not announced. ABC News reported that Redwood was expected to present on thimerosal at a vaccine-advisory meeting. A citation in her planned presentation was challenged by the study’s named author and later removed from a revised version.
existing_copy_for_context_only.long: In June 2025, Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. hired Lyn Redwood, although the department did not identify her exact role. ABC News reported that Redwood was expected to present at an Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices meeting about thimerosal, a preservative still used in some flu vaccines but removed from routine childhood vaccines in 2001. Her planned presentation cited a 2008 rat study under the name of Robert Berman, a professor emeritus at the University of California, Davis. Berman told ABC he had not written the paper and that his research did not make the claims attributed to it. The citation was removed from a revised presentation. Redwood had previously attributed her son’s autism to vaccine-related mercury exposure; that claim conflicts with scientific evidence that vaccines do not cause autism. The episode raised questions about the evidence planned for the advisory meeting. The source account does not specify Redwood’s appointment duties
